habitat: One of the commonest birds in the region, in a wide range of habitats, often with Laughing Dove, and also in more arid country.
summary: A very common, locally abundant resident. The head is uniform and there is no eye-ring. Colour varies from very pallid to quite sooty-grey. The bill is black and the legs are dark red. In flight the outer tail feathers are white, as on the Laughing Dove, but the mantle and wing coverts are greyish, not cinnamon. The call is a harsh, repeated “work harder, work harder”, and a snarling kerrr on landing.

similar.note: Laughing Dove has no black collar and a cinnamon mantle. Cape Turtle Dove has white outer tail feathers and a greyish mantle.
African Mourning Dove has a yellow eye and a red eye-ring. Cape Turtle Dove has a uniform head and no eye-ring.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^17=131072 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 65536–262144.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Grey dove with a uniform head and no eye-ring. The collar is the ring of the English name; its colour was not stated in the description.
Uniform head, no eye-ring, black bill.
White outer tail feathers and a greyish mantle, not the cinnamon mantle of a Laughing Dove.

calls.description: A harsh, much-repeated “work harder, work harder”, and a snarling kerrr on landing. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from Kruger, near Skukuza. The filename is RNDove.
